notes: Built from the 1500 BCE map, adjusted to 1250.

The reign of Ramesses II (about 1279–1213): Egypt held Nubia beyond the Fourth Cataract and southern Canaan; after the battle of Kadesh (about 1274) and the treaty of about 1259, the line with the Hittites ran south of Kadesh.
The Hittite Empire held central Anatolia, the former Arzawa lands in the west and northern Syria; Assyria under Shalmaneser I had annexed Hanigalbat, the last of Mitanni.
Crete was Mycenaean from about 1450. In Europe the Urnfield cultures were spreading from the Danube.
Within about seventy years this world broke apart in the Late Bronze Age collapse. Dates this early are uncertain, often by decades.
The Shang ruled the Yellow River c. 1500 BCE; the Zhou came in 1046 BCE.
The source map repeats 1000 BCE here; the Levant c. 1500 BCE was Canaanite city-states under Egyptian rule.
Northern Mesopotamia was the Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni; Assyria was its vassal.
Urartu appears only c. 860 BCE.
The Aramaeans appear after 1100 BCE.
The Phrygians arrived after 1200 BCE; western Anatolia was Arzawa.
The kingdom of Saba dates from c. 1000 BCE.
The Urnfield culture begins c. 1300 BCE.
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
The Nordic Bronze Age had begun by about 1700 BCE.
Peoples named before or after their time are renamed for this date.
Mongolia is named for its peoples and cultures of the time, not for the disputed "Proto-Altaic" language theory; after the Xiongnu, the Xianbei.
Names respelled or dated correctly.
Peoples of the deep past are named for their time: early modern humans, the Iberomaurusian and Capsian cultures, foragers before farming and herding spread.
Before the first states: the Faiyum and Naqada cultures in Egypt, the A-Group in Nubia, Neolithic Crete; Cyprus is Alashiya.
The Caribbean islands were settled from about 5000 BCE (the Bahamas from about 700 CE): Archaic peoples, then the Saladoid peoples and the Taíno.
Andean and Amazonian peoples are named for their time.
North American cultures are named for their time; the Mississippi and Ohio valleys were the land of the Mississippian and Fort Ancient cultures (boxes approximate).
Central Asia and the forest-steppe are named for their peoples of the time; the Tarim Basin was a land of oasis city-states (lines approximate).
Early South American cultures are drawn where they lived (lines approximate).
Territories filed under the wrong realm are moved to their own (for example the islands of South-East Asia, Travancore and Cochin, Cochin China, Sardinia).
